summary: Ochoco NF summit lookout in Wheeler County: cab 1923, timber tower 1938, removed 1968; concrete footings remain and forest roads reach the summit.

facts.design: 14x14 ft cab on a treated timber L-4 tower (per register and firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1968 (register) or destroyed that year (firelookout.com); concrete footings remain on the summit per Oregon Hikers

staffing.status: last staffing found in sources: Eudora and Leora Houston in 1952; later staffing not described

access.note: Reached by National Forest roads; Outdoor Pilgrim describes a dirt road with no signs on the route and possible closures of some land access from December 1 to May 1 for bald eagles

visit.trail_note: Outdoor Pilgrim says the Rim Trailhead on NF-200, about 1.5 miles from the summit, is the most common place for hikers to park

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ochoco National Forest

Four-acre man-caused fire on Cottonwood Creek near Dayville, reported by the Spanish Peak lookout

Tower removed (register and Oregon Hikers); firelookout.com says destroyed

corrections.why: 6.1 m (20 ft) describes the cab after it was raised onto stilts in 1931, not the tower that replaced it in 1938. Register, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers give a 50 ft (15.2 m) tower; a 1938 newspaper item gives 40 ft (12.2 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1930. A 1923 Central Oregonian item, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers give 1923. The story uses 1923 and notes the register's date.
Register dates the 50 ft L-4 tower to 1939. A 1938 newspaper item, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers give 1938. The story uses 1938 and notes the register's 1939.
Register and Oregon Hikers say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story uses removed and reports firelookout.com's wording.

notes_for_editor: Tower size is unresolved: 1938 Central Oregonian items say 40 ft (the December 1938 item calls it a type CT-3 tower), while the register, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers say 50 ft L-4. facts.height_m uses 50 ft because three later sources agree; the story reports both. The firelookout.org county index lists this site in Wasco County; the register, firelookout.com and Outdoor Pilgrim say Wheeler, so Wheeler is used. The site today is described only by Oregon Hikers (undated page) and Outdoor Pilgrim (access); no source describes a structure. No photos added.
